description.value: The study investigated how positive, negative, and neutral facial affect modulate effective connectivity within a right-hemisphere prefrontal-amygdala network during dynamic face matching.

design.value: All participants completed a 6-min fMRI dynamic face-matching and shape-matching task with alternating face and shape blocks. Whole-brain GLM analyses were followed by subject-level dynamic causal modeling, random-effects family-wise Bayesian model selection, Bayesian model averaging, and group-level tests of connectivity parameters.

description.value: A group of 33 healthy volunteers; 33 participants completed the task and were included in the whole-brain analyses. One subject was excluded from the DCM analysis because no active voxels were found in the LPFC at the chosen threshold.

medical_condition.value: healthy volunteers; no subject reported any past or current psychiatric disorder

task_description.value: Participants were presented with triplets of emotional faces in positive, negative, and neutral valence blocks and with polygons in shape blocks. In each 4-s trial, a dynamic target item was shown above two static probe images, and participants matched the target by facial expression or number of vertices.

design_type.value: alternating block design with dynamic 4-s trials

instructions.value: Subjects were instructed to match either the left or the right static item at the bottom with the dynamic item on top and to press either the left or the right button with their dominant hand on a response-pad to indicate their choice as soon as they recognized which probe matched.

stimuli.value: Face images came from the Radboud face database and included happy, surprised, neutral, sad, and disgusted facial expressions. Positive blocks used happy, surprised, and neutral faces; negative blocks used sad and disgusted faces; neutral blocks used neutral and surprised faces. Shapes were polygons with three to eight vertices superimposed on a whirled face. Target faces and shapes were dynamically morphed during each trial, whereas probe images remained static.

description.value: Functional images were acquired with a multiband echoplanar images (EPIs) sequence. Before the actual data acquisition, five dummy scans were acquired to establish steady-state conditions.

instrument.value: Philips Achieva 3 Tesla scanner (Philips Medical Systems) using a 32-channel head coil

description.value: After performing the task, a T1-weighted anatomic image was acquired for each subject and used for coregistration and normalization of functional data with a 3D magnetization-prepared rapid gradient-echo sequence (MP-RAGE).

description.value: Preprocessing included slice-timing correction, realignment, coregistration, and segmentation. Functional data were normalized to MNI-152 template space using deformations derived from segmentation, resampled to 2-mm isometric voxels, and smoothed with a 6-mm FWHM Gaussian kernel.

model_settings.value: Individual onset and length of each 4-s trial were modeled for face-matching and shape-matching. The final whole-brain GLM included regressors for all faces, positive faces, negative faces, neutral faces, and shapes, plus six realignment parameters as nuisance regressors.
The face-matching > shape-matching contrast files from each subject were entered into a one-sample t test.

A second-level repeated measures ANOVA was performed across the positive, negative, and neutral valence conditions. Cluster-based family-wise error correction used pFWEc = 0.05 with an uncorrected voxel-wise cluster-defining threshold of pCTD = 0.001.

The neural model included endogenous coupling parameters in matrix A, modulatory parameters for experimental inputs in matrix B, and direct driving inputs in matrix C. The four-region model comprised the LPFC, MPFC, AMY, and FFA. Bidirectional intrinsic connections were specified between MPFC and AMY, MPFC and LPFC, FFA and LPFC, and FFA and AMY; all possible intrinsic connectivity patterns between LPFC and AMY were included. Valence modulation was varied across MPFC-LPFC and MPFC-AMY connections, producing 256 models.

The 256 DCMs were grouped into four families: no contextual modulation (1 model), bottom-up modulation (15 models), top-down modulation (15 models), and bidirectional modulation (225 models). Expected posterior probabilities and exceedance probabilities were computed for model families.

estimator.value: free energy as a lower-bound approximation to log-model evidence

model_type.value: Bayesian model averaging followed by one-sample t tests

model_settings.value: Parameters were averaged across models weighted by posterior model probability. Averaged endogenous and modulatory parameter estimates were tested for consistency across subjects with one-sample t tests. Multiple comparisons were controlled using the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure with adjusted pFDRc < 0.05.
